title: Unify fallback resolver and DSL schema linter for region/tier routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
The current routing policy stack has several overlapping components: a legacy DSL parser, multiple ad-hoc validators, and a separate runtime resolver for fallback model variants and region/tier selection. This has led to inconsistent behavior across deployments (hosted vs Dedicated/Private), subtle incompatibilities during canary rollouts, and brittle migrations when model variants change.

Scope of this ticket:
- Design and implement a consolidated policy compiler pipeline that performs: 1) deterministic schema validation for the routing DSL, 2) an explicit fallback-resolver IR (intermediate representation) for region selection, tier routing, and model-variant fallback, and 3) a linter that flags or auto-fixes invalid/ambiguous rules.
- Provide a compatibility shim so existing policy JSON/YAML continue to run while flagged for migration.
- Add CI enforcement: new linter rules must run in policy-authoring pipelines and fail PRs for critical safety errors.
- Implement feature-flagged staged rollout for the new compiler (flag: new_policy_compiler).

Design highlights / constraints:
- DSL must express: geo selectors (region, country, continent), tier predicates (tier == "premium" / tier in [..]), capacity-aware routing hints, and ordered fallback chains for model variants (e.g., {preferred: rtx4090-quant, fallback: rtx3090-quant, last_resort: cpu-quant}).
- Schema validator must detect: unknown fields, ambiguous match predicates (overlapping region selectors), unreachable fallbacks, and circular fallback graphs.
- Linter should surface severity levels: ERROR for schema violations that could change routing behavior, WARN for cost/latency anti-patterns (e.g., very wide geo match leading to cross-region egress), and INFO for style suggestions.
- Runtime resolver generated by the compiler must be compact (small AST) so the hot path adds <1% p99 latency overhead compared to current resolver. It should support precomputed region maps and simple caches keyed by route+customer+region.
- Backwards compatibility: existing routing rules continue to be compiled by the compatibility shim; the new compiler emits warnings for deprecated constructs and provides automated migration hints.

Migration plan:
1) Implement schema and linter as a library inside policy-engine (unit-tested).
2) Land linter in policy-authoring CI; policy PRs start failing for ERROR-level violations.
3) Enable new_policy_compiler in staging for 25% of traffic with automatic fallback to legacy resolver on mismatch.
4) Run a two-week canary, measure routing correctness (golden tests) and latency/regressions.
5) Gradually increase rollout and provide teams with a migration report listing deprecated rules.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for DSL parsing and schema errors.
- Golden fixture set: 200 real customer-ish policies that should compile to expected IR outputs.
- E2E in staging: verify region selection for synthetic traffic across all logged regions; verify tier routing and variant fallbacks in failure scenarios (simulated capacity loss).
- Perf bench: measure p50/p95/p99 for resolver on representative token sequences; budget is <1% added p99 latency and no more than 5% CPU increase on serving nodes.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- UI changes to Console (separate PM/UI ticket will add rule authoring helpers).
- Dedicated autoscaling algorithms (we will expose hooks, not implement autoscaler changes).
acceptance_criteria: Schema validator accepts current canonical policy set (no false positives) and correctly rejects malformed policies with clear messages.
Linter produces ERROR for breaking constructs and warns for anti-patterns; CI pipeline fails on ERROR-level lint for policy PRs.
Compatibility shim preserves routing behavior for all policies in the staging corpus when new_policy_compiler is disabled.
New compiler feature-flag can be enabled and disabled without losing requests; staged rollout completed to 25% traffic and validated by golden tests.
Perf benchmarks show <1% p99 latency regression and within CPU budget on standard serving profiles.
Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence (links in attachments) and a migration report generated after canary.
At least two internal teams have migrated one rule each and confirmed behavior parity in their dev environments.
